before_findings: Autonomous conservative resolver was absent from scheduled sync task path.
Terminal prior reviews were ignored by queue_conflict_idempotently; every later scan could create a new OPEN row for the same conflict.
DQ ran after service job finalization in the Celery task wrapper.
after: REVIEW GENERATION WITH SEMANTIC FINGERPRINT / TERMINAL-CONFLICT LOOKUP
after_behavior: Successful jobs invoke resolve_post_sync_reviews in the existing source transaction.
Unchanged conflicts emit one SYSTEM_REEVALUATION per fingerprint per job and do not create a new actionable row.
Material source/canonical/evidence changes receive a distinct fingerprint and remain eligible for current reevaluation.
The service-level DQ run is persisted before final job state; task wrapper skips duplicate DQ when the job metrics contain POST_SYNC_DQ_RUN_ID.
Non-successful completed scans retain the task-level fast DQ fallback.
